verdicts.evidence: readFileSync(p, ''): the empty-string encoding is falsy, Node returns a Buffer (checked: Buffer.isBuffer = true, no throw). RegExp.test coerces its argument through String(buf) = buf.toString(), whose default encoding IS utf8 — the same bytes→string function as the 'utf8' read. Sensitivity control: the input that would make the two forms diverge would be a file where String(buffer) differs from the utf8 decode; impossible, both paths are buf.toString('utf8'). Checked on the most hostile input (latin-1 bytes invalid in utf8): String(readFileSync(p, '')) === readFileSync(p, 'utf8') → true. The exception path (EISDIR/EACCES) throws before the encoding is consulted: identical catch. Empirical battery of 4 fixtures (standard rejected DRAFT, latin-1 bytes, indented status, mid-line mention): CLI and function outputs identical between shipped and mutated.
